newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Qantas looks at flying out of NZ's Hamilton.
newsitem.headline: Qantas looks at flying out of NZ's Hamilton.

text.p: Australian national airline Qantas says it may start trans-Tasman flights from Hamilton but will eye the winter travel market first, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Friday.

Regional general manager Paul Donovan, in Hamilton on Thursday to meet airport officials and Mayor Margaret Evans, said he did not want to build expectations but Qantas was interested in Hamilton as a distribution hub for a lot more than tourism.
He said he and two managers who accompanied him were "delighted" with the airport.
"The airport is great. There is nothing you would have to do if contemplating an operation," said Donovan, whose visit was to familiarise himself with the Waikato region.
Asked if Qantas was interested in coming to Hamilton, he said: "Absolutely".
"There are opportunities in the area and in the South Island. There may even be opportunities for linking them up."
Hamilton's pioneer trans-Tasman airline Kiwi said before it failed in September that it was talking to Qantas about strengthening its market. A rescue deal could not be put together in time.
Donovan said he was mindful of what Air New Zealand's Freedom airline was doing in the Hamilton-trans-Tasman market. There was already a viable market in the city with eight flights a week.
A focus would be how to generate a strong market on both sides of the Tasman.
He believed Freedom saw itself as an "out-bound" service -- taking people out of the region.
Qantas would be keen to work with the tourism market and Waikato people to bring Australians to the region.
